newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH BAN PIG MARKETS AS SWINE FEVER SPREADS.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH BAN PIG MARKETS AS SWINE FEVER SPREADS.

text.p: The Dutch ministry for Agricultural Affairs said on Monday it had banned concentrating pigs in any one place throughout the whole country from Tuesday, February 18.
"This implies that that pigs from various companies are no longer allowed to be taken to export centres. All pig markets have been suspended," the ministry said in a statement.

It added that the measure was necessary to reduce the risk of spreading the swine fever epidemic currently hitting the southern Netherlands. All transport bans which were imposed earlier remain valid, the ministry said.
Earlier on Monday, the Belgian authorities decided to slaughter 12,000 pigs to prevent the contagious disease from spreading to Belgium from the Netherlands.
So far, 17 cases of swine fever have been discovered in the Netherlands. The Dutch Farm Ministry has ordered the slaughter of over 35,000 pigs in the areas which are affected.
European Union inspectors arrived on Sunday to assess the Dutch response to the swine fever outbreak.
On Wednesday, the European Union's Standing Veterinary Committee backed a ban on exports of pigs from seven Dutch districts.
Earlier, the U.S. halted imports of Dutch pork products and Poland closed its borders to all imports of Dutch pigs, pork and pork products.
Last year, the Netherlands exported almost a million tonnes of pigs and pork products, about 60 percent of its production, bringing in around 5.1 billion guilders ($2.7 billion).
Of 14 million pigs in the country, a fifth are in the "Westelijk Peelgebied" area of the southern Netherlands where swine fever has broken out.
Swine fever, last detected in the Netherlands in 1992, is a highly contagious disease, but is not harmful to humans. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
